newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan mulling financial deregulation by 2001 - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan mulling financial deregulation by 2001 - MOF.

text.p: Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Monday that his ministry will aim to implement measures to make Japan's financial markets freer, fairer and more global by 2001.

Mitsuzuka told a news conference that Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto unveiled at a meeting with him today a set of plans for reforming Japan's financial system, including the liberalisation of foreign exchange transactions.
The following are the main points of the reform plans, most of which are currently being discussed by government advisory councils.
For the creation of freer markets:
- Banks, securities houses and insurance firms should be allowed to enter each others' business areas.
- Banks and other financial institutions should be allowed to deal in more products in a bid to meet a wide range of investor needs.
- Japan will look into the liberalisation of financial market commission fees.
- Participation in foreign exchange transactions, currently limited to banks authorised by the government, should be liberalised.
- Considering the effective use of individual savings, which now total 1,200 trillion yen.
For the creation of fairer markets:
- Asking financial institutions to make satisfactory disclosure of information to investors and depositors, and setting up rules to make market participants responsible for their investment.
- More severe punishment for market participants for violation of rules regarding their involvement in the markets.
For the creation of more internationalised markets:
- Promotion of investment in financial derivatives in Japan by the revision of the Japanese accounting system and relevant laws to meet global standards.
- Establishment of a supervisory system on a global scale. The Group of Seven industrialised nations have confirmed the setting up of such a system.

Mitsuzuka said in a statement: "While proceeding with the disposal of problem loans, Japan aims to rejuvenate its financial markets (and turn it into) an international market equivalent to that in New York and London by 2001."
